correctness.rationale: The full matrix lemma and rank-one normalization were checked: N=uv^T with v^T u=0, nonzero beta=v_1u_3, normalize u3=1 and recover x=N11/beta,y=N21/beta. This proves polynomial inverse and rank-one square-zero for every (x,y). Repeated split eigenvalues contradict either J^2 !=0 when D=0 or rank(D+lambda I)>=2 from invertible J+lambda I plus rank-one N. Pairwise distinct zero-sum triples number (q-1)(q-2)/6; total square-zero matrices q^4+q^3-q. Independent F4 complete rank-one enumeration found 315 nonzero square-zero N and exactly 16 diagonalizable perturbations in a single q^2 fiber. This finite check does not imply the theorem for all q.

final_claim: For J3(0) over each finite characteristic-two field F_q, all diagonalizable D=J+N with N squared zero have three distinct nonzero eigenvalues summing to zero. Every admissible spectral fiber is scheme-theoretically an affine plane A2 with q^2 points, giving q^2(q-1)(q-2)/6 ordered decompositions and density tending to 1/6 among square-zero perturbations.
limitations: Characteristic two only, ground-field diagonalizable, fixed Jordan basis; actual decompositions not similarity orbits.
